log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon
|-damage|p2a: Kingambit|87/100|[from] ability: Rough Skin|[of] p1a: Garchomp

decisions.thought:
Lead: 44% BRING: ninetalesalola, 29% BRING: garchomp, 13% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 29% BRING: garchomp, 29% BRING: rotomwash, 29% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 3: 57% BRING: garchomp, 31% BRING: gholdengo, 8% BRING: scizor

Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out, which blunts Garchomp and Scizor's physical attacks. Garchomp gives fast Mega Garchomp pressure with Earthquake and Stone Edge. Kingambit adds a strong Dark/Steel physical threat that hits Ninetales-Alola and Gholdengo hard.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to settle on my three leads here. Looking at the opponent's team of Garchomp, Rotom-Wash, Scizor, Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Ninetales-Alola against my own squad of Incineroar, Garchomp, Gholdengo, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Archaludon, I'm weighing which picks give the best matchups—Incineroar for utility, Garchomp as a fast mega threat, and Kingambit for pressuring their Steel and Ghost types.

I'll settle on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Kingambit as the final team, leading with Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out utility.

decisions.thought: 92% MOVE: auroraveil, 6% SWITCH: rotomwash, 1% MOVE: encore

Ninetales-Alola is almost certainly faster than my Incineroar (80 Speed), so it would act first. Fake Out is legal only on my first turn and flinches the target, which stops Ninetales from moving this turn. That gives Incineroar a free turn to set up a Flare Blitz next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: For turn 1 I'm considering Fake Out from Incineroar, since it's legal and flinches Ninetales-Alola, preventing it from acting. But Ninetales outspeeds Incineroar, so I need to weigh whether it could attack first before I can follow up with a super-effective Flare Blitz.

decisions.thought: 93% MOVE: auroraveil, 3% MOVE: moonblast, 2% SWITCH: rotomwash

Incineroar is slower than Ninetales-Alola, but Flare Blitz is super effective against Ice/Fairy and should knock out or nearly knock out the 84% target. Fake Out has already been used, so Flare Blitz is the strongest option this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since Flare Blitz is super effective against Ninetales-Alola's Ice typing, I'm estimating the damage using Incineroar's boosted attack against Ninetales' defense, factoring in its current HP of around 151.

decisions.thought: 66% SWITCH: rotomwash, 16% SWITCH: garchomp, 12% MOVE: moonblast

Ninetales-Alola is at 16% and outspeeds Incineroar, but it can't KO Incineroar (169 HP) in one hit. Flare Blitz is super effective and should knock it out even through Aurora Veil. Protect or switching only delays the KO.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Ninetales is down to 16% with Aurora Veil active, but it's slower than Incineroar, so even with the veil's damage reduction, a super-effective Flare Blitz should finish it off easily.

decisions.thought: 70% MOVE: hydropump, 30% MOVE: voltswitch, 0% MOVE: willowisp

Flare Blitz is resisted by Rotom-Wash's Water typing and costs 33% recoil, so it's a poor trade. Parting Shot cuts Rotom's Attack and Sp. Atk, its main offensive stats, and pivots Incineroar out safely.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's Flare Blitz won't do much since Rotom-Wash resists Fire with its Water typing, and Rotom outspeeds, so it could threaten back with Hydro Pump, Thunderbolt, or Will-O-Wisp.

I'm considering switch options: Kingambit is decently neutral against Rotom-Wash's typing, though nothing hits it super effectively. Garchomp's Earthquake is useless against Rotom's Levitate, and Water actually hits Garchomp's Ground typing hard, so that's risky too. Parting Shot from Incineroar could be a safer play, weakening Rotom's offenses while giving us a free switch into something better suited.

decisions.thought: Incineroar fainted, so I must switch. Garchomp outspeeds Rotom-Wash (169 vs at most 151) and can threaten Mega Garchomp, while Earthquake is useless into Levitate. Hydro Pump hits Garchomp super effectively, but Garchomp's speed and Dragon/Rock damage make it the better choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar down, I need to pick a switch. Garchomp's Ground typing is useless against Rotom-Wash since it has Levitate, so Earthquake won't land, and Garchomp would also be vulnerable to Hydro Pump from its Water side.

Kingambit looks safer: Dark/Steel takes neutral damage from Water and Electric, and with Supreme Overlord boosting its massive Attack, Kowtow Cleave could threaten Rotom-Wash hard.

Comparing speeds, Garchomp outruns Rotom and could set up Swords Dance before attacking with Outrage or Stone Edge, though Hydro Pump back would hurt given Garchomp's weakness to Water. Mega Garchomp seems like the strongest option if it can switch in safely and start sweeping.

decisions.thought: 61% MOVE: hydropump, 31% MOVE: willowisp, 5% MOVE: voltswitch

Earthquake is useless because Rotom-Wash's Levitate grants Ground immunity. Outrage is a 100% accuracy neutral Dragon hit, and Mega Garchomp's much higher Attack should maximize damage. Mega speed drops but likely still keeps Garchomp ahead of most Rotom-Wash builds.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Rotom-Wash's Levitate ability makes it immune to Ground, so Earthquake would do nothing despite the type advantage—I should avoid that move. Stone Edge is neutral against both Electric and Water, so it's not a great option either.

I'm weighing Mega Garchomp's Outrage instead—Dragon type is neutral against Electric/Water, but Garchomp's raw Attack stat of 182 could still deal solid damage. I need to check whether Mega evolving actually boosts stats enough here and account for the Aurora Veil halving physical damage, plus confirm Rotom-Wash's current HP and defensive bulk against this attack.

Doing the speed math more carefully: Mega Garchomp still clocks in around 144 speed, which could land either above or below Rotom's max roll of 151, so the outspeed outcome is genuinely uncertain. Still, Mega Outrage looks appealing since Rotom's Hydro Pump isn't super effective against Garchomp either way, and Garchomp's bulky HP pool should let it absorb a hit if it ends up moving second.

decisions.thought: 99% MOVE: hydropump, 1% SWITCH: garchomp, 0% MOVE: voltswitch

Only one legal action is available: Outrage. Rotom-Wash is immune to Ground (Levitate), so Earthquake is not an option anyway. Garchomp is faster and Outrage is super effective on Rotom-Wash, so it's the move.
Garchomp has fainted, so the only legal action is switching in Kingambit. I must pick the single listed option.
88% SWITCH: garchomp, 6% MOVE: willowisp, 3% MOVE: hydropump

Rotom-Wash is at 28% (about 44 HP), and Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave gets a boost from Supreme Overlord with two fainted allies. Its 100% accuracy means it should KO through Aurora Veil. Sucker Punch could go first, but it fails if Rotom switches or protects, so Kowtow Cleave is the more reliable pick. Iron Head is weak here because Steel is resisted by Water.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking type matchups against Rotom-Wash: Kingambit's Dark moves hit neutrally, but Iron Head is Steel-type, which gets quartered against the Electric/Water typing since both types resist Steel.

At roughly 44 HP, I'm weighing Kowtow Cleave against Sucker Punch -- Kowtow Cleave boosted by Supreme Overlord and the attack item is reliable and accuracy-proof, while Sucker Punch hits harder but risks failing if Rotom doesn't attack. Speed order matters too: if Rotom outpaces and fires Hydro Pump first, it won't be enough to KO Kingambit's 177 HP, so Kingambit should still land the finishing blow regardless of move choice.

Given the risk that Sucker Punch fails on a switch or Protect, I'm settling on Kowtow Cleave as the more consistent kill.

decisions.thought: 100% MOVE: earthquake, 0% MOVE: stoneedge, 0% MOVE: swordsdance

Kingambit is slower than Garchomp, but Kowtow Cleave is still the strongest option, and it never misses. Aurora Veil halves the damage, so the hit may not knock Garchomp out, but it is the highest-damage play. Sucker Punch does less damage and only works if Garchomp attacks.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit has two fainted allies (Garchomp and Incineroar), giving Supreme Overlord a +20% power boost. I'm calculating Kowtow Cleave's damage with STAB and Black Glasses against the opposing Garchomp.

Factoring STAB and item boosts gets damage to around 127, close to Garchomp's remaining HP. Sucker Punch gives Kingambit priority if Garchomp attacks, so the speed comparison matters less than whether Garchomp commits to an attacking move versus status.
